content: Challenges: In training a classifier to distinguish between user and non-user tweets, we should ideally have an equal amount of examples of both classes. User tweets are simply all the tweets from that user's Twitter account, and measure perhaps in the thousands. Indeed, the number of tweets per user per day is limited to 2400 per day by current Twitter policy (https://help.twitter.com/en/rules-and-policies/twitter-limits). The negative examples consist of all tweets written by other Twitter users, a total of approximately 500 million per day (https://business.twitter.com). Thus there is an extreme class imbalance between user and non-user tweets. Moreover, the nature of language used on Twitter does not conform to formal syntactic or semantic rules. The sentences tend to be highly unstructured, and the vocabulary is not restricted to a particular dictionary.
